title: QBR - Novara Financial - Health Check
next_steps: Maya to send month-to-date usage + cost export
Schedule Dedicated capacity scoping call w/ infra team
Share SOC 2 and network diagram links
SE to run a 1k-request latency/cost benchmark and share results
action_items: Maya: send monthly usage + cost dashboard export by 2026-11-13
Ethan: set up dedicated scoping call and invite Novara infra by 2026-11-18

summary: Quarterly review focusing on usage trends, rising latency on peak windows, cost drivers (embeddings + chat traffic), and roadmap alignment for Dedicated capacity and VPC options. Action items include sharing detailed cost export, scheduling a Dedicated scoping call, and running targeted latency/cost benchmarks.
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Patel: hey everyone thanks for joining, we'll kick off the QBR for Novara, i've got Ethan from our SE team and Jamal from CSM. how's everyone doing?
[00:12] Sofia Ruiz: good thanks Maya, excited to go through usage, we've noticed some latency blips during EOD batch windows.
[00:22] Daniel Park: yeah we've seen p95 go up to 1.8s for chat routes around 20:00 UTC when batch jobs run.
[00:30] Ethan Chen: ok, thanks for that context. quick agenda — usage/cost, reliability, security, and next steps. we'll also talk about Dedicated capacity options since you flagged predictability.
[00:42] Leila Morgan: sounds good. also would like to understand regressions — we've had a couple prompts change outputs after the last model rollout.
[00:50] Maya Patel: yeah we'll cover model rollouts and evals, and how rollback / canary works in the console.
[01:05] Jamal Ortiz: i'll share the QBR deck after but just call out we pulled month over month usage — embeddings are up 3x due to new feature.
[01:15] Sofia Ruiz: that explains cost. embeddings are driving most spend, chat traffic also increased. can you show the breakdown?
[01:22] Maya Patel: sure — i'll send the detailed export as a csv, but high level we saw 62% of tokens attributable to embeddings and reranking during Oct. when you add high sequence lengths for some of your prompts that bumps cost.
[01:35] Daniel Park: right, and our infra team is worried about latency during those spikes. are there batching or kv cache knobs we can tune?
[01:44] Ethan Chen: yes, we have a few levers — intelligent batching, prefix/KV caching for repeated contexts, and aggressive quantization for lower cost models. for your workload i'd recommend keeping low-latency routes on hosted for critical requests and offload large embedding batches to dedicated pools or scheduled jobs.
[02:03] Leila Morgan: what about Dedicated capacity — we need commit vs burst options, isolation, and predictable SLOs.
[02:12] Maya Patel: Dedicated gives reserved GPU pools, autoscaling with burst allowed, and SLA backing. we can do canary rollouts and pin model versions. there was a typo in my notes — sometimes the console shows 'Redwood Dedicate' in auto transcripts haha.
[02:25] Sofia Ruiz: (laughs) ok. security — Omar, your questions?
[02:30] Omar Haddad: yes. we need SOC 2 Type II evidence, KMS integration for customer-managed keys, SSO via SAML, RBAC, and audit logs for all inference requests. how mature is the private deployment offering?
[02:46] Ethan Chen: we support VPC and on-prem for private deployments, KMS/HSM integrations, SAML SSO and granular RBAC. our SOC 2 and ISO docs are in the security pack — i'll share links. audit logs capture request metadata and you can configure retention.
[03:01] Daniel Park: if we move embeddings to Dedicated, will data leave our VPC?
[03:06] Maya Patel: for Dedicated hosted in our cloud, data is logically isolated but network egress exists in our infra. For full isolation you can look at Private (VPC or on-prem) where you control networking.
[03:19] Sofia Ruiz: cost tradeoffs — Dedicated has committed pricing but requires forecast. How do we avoid overcommit?
[03:27] Jamal Ortiz: we can structure a hybrid — reserved capacity for steady state, burst into hosted or spot pools. Redwood Optimize also gives recommendations on batching and quant profiles to reduce unit cost.
[03:40] Leila Morgan: the rollout regression — we saw degraded output after a minor model swap last month. can you walk through evals and rollback?
[03:48] Ethan Chen: sure — console supports per-route rollouts, A/B testing, and automatic fallback. run your eval sets (you mentioned top-10 prompts) and we can alert on quality regressions. if regression detected, system automatically fallbacks to previous pinned model if configured.
[04:05] Daniel Park: ideal — can you run a sandbox benchmark of 1k requests across our top routes to measure p95 and cost?
[04:12] Ethan Chen: yes, we'll run that. expect separate results for hosted baseline and Dedicated pool.
[04:20] Sofia Ruiz: network/throughput questions — our security wants to see network diagrams and whether there's any persistent KV cache stored off-node.
[04:29] Maya Patel: KV cache is ephemeral to inference nodes; for Dedicated we can provision nodes within a VPC or private infra. network diagrams will be included with the SOC docs link.
[04:41] Omar Haddad: also need clarification on encryption at rest for logs and model artifacts.
[04:47] Ethan Chen: logs and artifact storage can be encrypted with customer-managed keys in Private deployments; in hosted we use provider-managed keys but SOC docs explain controls.
[04:57] Leila Morgan: ok thanks. timeline — if we want Dedicated by Q1, what's next?
[05:03] Maya Patel: next step is a scoping call with infra to size pools and commit levels, run a PoC if you want to validate latency/cost, and then contract work with our sales ops.
[05:15] Daniel Park: can we get a proposal with commit tiers and expected unit economics based on our usage?
[05:21] Jamal Ortiz: yes we'll prepare a draft proposal — Maya will own that.
[05:27] Sofia Ruiz: one more — monitoring for regressions. does Redwood integrate with our existing Datadog?
[05:33] Ethan Chen: we have tracing hooks and exports to Datadog/prometheus. plus per-route dashboards in the console.
[05:40] Leila Morgan: great. any blockers?
[05:43] Maya Patel: Omar had a few security clarifications, Sofia will provide prompt set, Ethan will run benchmarks, and we'll produce cost export.
[05:52] Jamal Ortiz: i'll summarize actions in an email.
[05:55] Sofia Ruiz: thanks all.
[06:00] Maya Patel: recap of next steps — i'll send usage + cost export, Ethan will run the 1k-request benchmark and set up scoping call, Omar to confirm encryption/KMS requirements, and Sofia to upload top prompt set. we'll aim to reconvene after scoping with proposal.
[06:18] Daniel Park: thanks, that works.
[06:22] Maya Patel: thanks everyone — closing early to let folks move on.
[06:28] (end)
